problem_text: Let f : C[x,y] -> C[x,y], x -> p(x) + ay, y -> x, where a in C, a != 0, p(x) in C[x] have degree > 1, p subset C[x,y] be a prime ideal. If height p = 1, then f(p) != p.
solution_text: Proof: Since C[x,y] is a UFD, every height-1 prime ideal is principal, generated by an irreducible polynomial. So p = (g) for some irreducible g in C[x,y]. The map f is an automorphism (its inverse sends x -> y, y -> (x - p(y))/a, which is well-defined since a != 0). Suppose for contradiction that f(p) = p. Then (f(g)) = (g), so f(g) = c*g for some nonzero constant c in C*. Iterating, f^n(g) = c^n * g, which has constant degree deg(g) for all n. Now f^n(x) has degree d^n where d = deg(p) > 1 (by induction: f(x) = p(x)+ay has degree d, f^2(x) = p(p(x)+ay)+ax has degree d^2, etc.). Also f^n(y) = f^{n-1}(x), so f^n(g) = g(f^n(x), f^{n-1}(x)). Case 1: g involves x (deg_x(g) > 0). Then g(f^n(x), f^{n-1}(x)) has degree growing like d^n, contradicting deg(f^n(g)) = deg(g). Case 2: g = g(y) only. Then f(g) = g(x), and f(g) = c*g requires g(x) = c*g(y), impossible for non-constant g. Contradiction in both cases. QED.
solution_summary: Use UFD structure to reduce to principal ideal (g), then f(g)=cg by automorphism. Iterate to get f^n(g)=c^n*g with constant degree, but deg(f^n(x))=d^n grows unboundedly since deg p > 1. If g involves x, degree of f^n(g) grows — contradiction. If g=g(y), then f(g)=g(x)≠cg(y) — contradiction.
answer: f(𝔭) ≠ 𝔭 for any height-1 prime ideal 𝔭 in C[x,y] under the automorphism f: x↦p(x)+ay, y↦x with a≠0 and deg p > 1

key_insight: Iterating f makes deg(f^n(g)) grow like (deg p)^n, but f(g)=cg forces f^n(g)=c^n*g with constant degree — contradiction. The translation from ideal equality to degree arithmetic is the key move.

Since g is irreducible and f(g) is also irreducible (automorphism preserves irreducibility), they differ by a unit: f(g) = cg for some c ∈ C*.
